dysbiosis.description: Dysbiosis refers to an imbalanced microbial community structure associated with disease. Typically characterized by reduced diversity, loss of beneficial SCFA producers, and expansion of facultative anaerobes or pathobionts.

inflammatory_bowel_disease.description: IBD (Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis) is consistently associated with depletion of butyrate producers (Faecalibacterium, Roseburia) and expansion of mucin-degrading or pro-inflammatory species.

obesity.description: Obesity-associated microbiome typically shows altered Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio, depletion of Akkermansia and Christensenella, and enhanced energy harvest capacity.

type_2_diabetes.description: T2D microbiome is characterized by reduced butyrate producers, increased LPS biosynthesis, and elevated branched-chain amino acid production. Akkermansia depletion is a consistent finding.

colorectal_cancer.description: CRC shows enrichment of oral-origin bacteria (Fusobacterium, Parvimonas) and enterotoxigenic Bacteroides fragilis. These promote tumor progression via immune evasion and DNA damage.

antibiotic_associated_diarrhea.description: Antibiotic exposure collapses gut diversity, depletes colonization resistance, and enables C. difficile expansion. Loss of bile acid-metabolizing species is a key mechanism.

depression_gut_brain_axis.description: Depression is associated with depletion of butyrate producers and specific genera (Coprococcus, Dialister). The gut-brain axis involves tryptophan metabolism, SCFA signaling, and vagal afferents.

allergic_diseases.description: Early-life microbiome maturation delays are linked to asthma, eczema, and food allergies. Depletion of Bifidobacterium and specific Clostridia clusters impairs immune tolerance development.

liver_disease.description: Cirrhosis and NAFLD show gut dysbiosis with oral bacteria translocation, Enterobacteriaceae expansion, and endotoxemia driving hepatic inflammation.

cardiovascular_disease.description: CVD microbiome contributes via trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) production from choline/carnitine, chronic LPS-driven inflammation, and altered bile acid metabolism.

non_alcoholic_fatty_liver_disease.description: NAFLD/NASH microbiome shows increased ethanol-producing bacteria, Enterobacteriaceae expansion, and decreased butyrate producers. Endotoxemia drives hepatic inflammation and steatosis progression.

alzheimers_disease.description: AD microbiome shows reduced Bacteroides and butyrate producers, increased pro-inflammatory taxa. Bacterial amyloid and LPS may contribute to neuroinflammation via gut-brain axis.

parkinsons_disease.description: PD is associated with reduced Prevotella and butyrate producers, Enterobacteriaceae expansion. Gut dysfunction precedes motor symptoms. Alpha-synuclein pathology may originate in the gut.

rheumatoid_arthritis.description: RA shows enrichment of Prevotella copri and Collinsella aerofaciens. Bacterial citrullination may trigger anti-CCP autoantibodies. Oral-gut axis involvement is increasingly recognized.

chronic_kidney_disease.description: CKD microbiome produces uremic toxins (p-cresol sulfate, indoxyl sulfate, TMAO) that the failing kidneys cannot clear. Beneficial SCFA producers are depleted.

irritable_bowel_syndrome.description: IBS microbiome shows mild diversity loss, depletion of Bifidobacterium and butyrate producers, and enrichment of gas-producing Dorea/Ruminococcus; subtype (IBS-D vs IBS-C) profiles differ.

metabolic_syndrome.description: Metabolic syndrome associates with low bacterial gene richness, Akkermansia depletion, and a pro-inflammatory LPS-rich community driving metabolic endotoxemia.

hypertension.description: Hypertension cohorts show reduced SCFA-producing taxa and enrichment of Prevotella/Klebsiella; acetate and butyrate signalling via GPR41/43/109A modulates blood pressure.

autism_spectrum_disorder.description: ASD gut profiles commonly show Prevotella depletion and Clostridium/Desulfovibrio enrichment; associations are confounded by diet selectivity and remain an active research area.

multiple_sclerosis.description: Multiple sclerosis is linked to reduced SCFA producers and altered Prevotella/Akkermansia balance, with proposed effects on Th17/Treg immune homeostasis.

celiac_disease.description: Celiac disease shows Bifidobacterium depletion and shifts in gluten-metabolising taxa; a gluten-free diet itself reshapes the community and confounds untreated-disease signatures.

asthma.description: Early-life depletion of Lachnospira/Faecalibacterium/Roseburia/Veillonella (the 'LRVF' signature) predicts asthma risk; SCFA-mediated immune regulation is the leading mechanistic hypothesis.

bacterial_vaginosis.description: BV is a shift from Lactobacillus crispatus dominance (CST I) to a diverse anaerobic community with Gardnerella biofilms; vaginal pH rises as lactate falls.

periodontal_disease.description: Periodontitis features a keystone-pathogen-driven dysbiotic biofilm (red complex: P. gingivalis, T. forsythia, T. denticola) sustained by inflammation-derived nutrients.

dental_caries.description: Carious lesions are dominated by acidogenic/aciduric taxa (S. mutans, Lactobacillus, Scardovia) whose fermentation acids demineralise enamel.
